trust_decision.summary: The 'safe' evaluator decides whether a filter-expression member access may read a prototype property (constructor/__proto__/__defineGetter__/__defineSetter__), by checking the property key against a Set in SafeEval.evalMemberExpression. A non-string computed key (e.g. an array) misses the Set lookup but is coerced to the blocked name at obj[prop].

landing_point.why: The advisory says 'safe eval RCE'. Safe-Script.js is the only safe evaluator, and line 127 is the only blocklist check, added by the previous advisory fix (commit 73ad72e).

fix_sites.entry_point: Public API JSONPath({path, json}) / new JSONPath(...).evaluate() (src/jsonpath.js:137, src/jsonpath.js:199) with a [?(expr)] filter or [(expr)] dynamic segment (src/jsonpath.js:456, src/jsonpath.js:471) and the default eval 'safe' (src/jsonpath.js:165, src/jsonpath.js:656-661); also the CLI bin/jsonpath-cli.js:29-32
Package exports and the CLI load the dist bundles (package.json:10-23, bin/jsonpath-cli.js:3). The fix regenerated all dist bundles (fix.diff:14-127)
fix_sites.module_kind: generated build artifact (rollup bundle of src), not hand-written source

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: dist/index-node-esm.js:1298-1307 (also dist/index-node-cjs.cjs:1300, dist/index-browser-esm.js:1299, dist/index-browser-umd.cjs:1305, minified bundles). This is a generated copy of the same function, rebuilt by rollup and committed, and it is what the CLI and package exports load. Weak as a task lever because the project's tests import src (test-helpers/node-env.js:7,13).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For O8: the report is about a non-string key slipping past the name blocklist. Reaching a prototype through a built-in accessor-lookup method and then reading that prototype's own 'constructor' (which the hasOwn exception allows by design) looks like a different, wider sandbox-escape class, not this bug's key-coercion issue.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Filters must still call prototype methods on data and sandbox values (e.g. ["book","books"].includes(@property), sandbox functions bound to their object), and must still read a data object's own key named 'constructor' (hasOwn exception). An over-broad fix that blocks non-own properties or all calls breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: non-computed identifier property (already a string, e.g. a.constructor)
computed array-literal key that stringifies to a blocked name (a[['constructor']]), the published case (fix.diff:784)
computed object key with an overridden toString returning a non-string, which String() now rejects (fix.diff:762-764)

O7_producer.where: src/jsonpath.js:645-661 compiles and caches the SafeScript per (eval mode, code); it is not a producer of the bypassing state

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Reaching a prototype object through non-blocked accessor-lookup builtins (__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__, via .call on the bound function), then reading that prototype's own 'constructor', which passes the hasOwn exception and reaches the Function constructor that evalCallExpression invokes.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different gadget from the report's key-coercion example. The hasOwn exception at src/Safe-Script.js:127 is intentional so that own 'constructor' keys in data keep working.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and function as the fix (src/Safe-Script.js:127 vs blocklist at :12-17; call sink at :152-159)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: No callee check in evalCallExpression. A Function-constructor guard exists only as commented-out code, so any route that yields Function reaches the sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Seen as defence in depth; the published fix closed the member-access route and left this commented out.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 35 lines below the fix

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An object-literal or spread evaluator (evalObjectExpression) that reads or assigns computed keys without the String() coercion and blocklist check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: jsep plugins (@jsep-plugin/object) add object literals. The maintainer already added evaluators per node type (ArrayExpression at :149), and would likely copy evalMemberExpression's raw key handling.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Member-target assignment (obj[key] = v) via a relaxed evalAssignmentExpression that writes computed keys without the blocklist.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The assignment plugin is already registered (src/Safe-Script.js:4,7). Only Identifier targets are allowed now, and supporting @.x = ... is a natural feature request.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second safe evaluator path (e.g. a 'safe' variant used for [(expr)] dynamic segments, or a cached precompiled evaluator) with its own copy of the member-access check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _eval already dispatches between several evaluator kinds, so adding a fast path for the dynamic-property segment at src/jsonpath.js:471 would be plausible.

O9_family: code injection / sandbox escape in an expression evaluator (CWE-94), prototype-property blocklist bypass by type confusion of the computed key

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js, pnpm/npm, mocha + chai, rollup (only needed for dist), eslint, c8
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.safe-eval.js (security tests at :249-293), run via 'mocha --require test-helpers/node-env.js' (package.json:133) against src for both the builtin vm and the node vm (test-helpers/node-env.js:7,13)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a typeof prop === 'string' guard or String(prop) before the BLOCKED_PROTO_PROPERTIES lookup at src/Safe-Script.js:127, leaving the hasOwn exception and the uncovered callee open.

out_of_scope_notes: README.md:179-183 says 'safe' has no effect in NodeJS, but src/jsonpath.js:656-661 uses SafeScript in Node too (doc drift, not pursued).
eval:'native' and custom eval callbacks/classes (src/jsonpath.js:662-674) run code natively by documented design; not this advisory's protection.
Computed member properties are evaluated without subs (src/Safe-Script.js:119), so a[x] with a variable key throws; a functional quirk, not pursued.
